Use a numbered stage marker to bind demand, capacity, and service level to lane count. -> supplies an inspectable output -> hands it to the next paragraph or section
Advance from capacity sizing to a separate risk-flow routing problem. -> supplies an inspectable output -> hands it to the next paragraph or section
Introduce the geometry/cost layer only after the operating pattern is defined. -> supplies an inspectable output -> hands it to the next paragraph or section
Close the preview with a named case and communication handoff. -> supplies an inspectable output -> hands it to the next paragraph or section
Establish the system-scale motivation before narrowing to a toll barrier. -> supplies an inspectable output -> hands it to the next paragraph or section
Name the local infrastructure object and its operational role. -> supplies an inspectable output -> hands it to the next paragraph or section
State the demand-capacity mismatch that creates queues. -> supplies an inspectable output -> hands it to the next paragraph or section
Turn the observed bottleneck into a design question. -> supplies an inspectable output -> hands it to the next paragraph or section
Organize prior work by traffic capacity, safety, and environmental effect. -> supplies an inspectable output -> hands it to the next paragraph or section
Identify the dominant literature branch before contrasting gaps. -> supplies an inspectable output -> hands it to the next paragraph or section
Add the safety branch and its simulation mechanisms. -> supplies an inspectable output -> hands it to the next paragraph or section
Concede prior contributions before naming the missing synthesis. -> supplies an inspectable output -> hands it to the next paragraph or section
Formulate the gap as an integration problem rather than absence of all research. -> supplies an inspectable output -> hands it to the next paragraph or section
Claim the paper's design scope after the gap is explicit. -> supplies an inspectable output -> hands it to the next paragraph or section
Assign traffic flow, capacity, and service level to the sizing branch. -> supplies an inspectable output -> hands it to the next paragraph or section
Assign maximum throughput and minimum risk to the routing branch. -> supplies an inspectable output -> hands it to the next paragraph or section
Assign braking and following distance to the footprint branch. -> supplies an inspectable output -> hands it to the next paragraph or section

global_organization_chain: toll-plaza safety, throughput, congestion, footprint, and cost decision
public-road motivation, mechanism, literature branches, synthesis gap, and four work packages
three design tensions, conditional assumptions, symbol interface, and overall flow
design-hour demand and single-lane service/departure capacity
M/G/K stay, queue length, delay, qualitative service levels, and intensity lookup
integer lane selection and demand sensitivity
directed graph abstraction with separate throughput and exposure-weighted risk objectives
arc bounds, node balances, scalarized objective, and augmenting-path labeling
worked booth capacities, 24-node topology, route groups, and reported accident rate
rear braking, two-vehicle safety distance, symmetric fan length, and plaza area
traffic-flow, autonomous-vehicle, and booth-composition scenario branches
New Jersey data collection, daily-flow reading, relaxed geometry, candidate design, and existing comparison
conclusion, explicit strengths/weaknesses, future extensions, and authority-facing advice
references, service-level annexes, capacity matrix, and implementation listings

only after positive language, organization, model, and visual retention does the final warning pass record arithmetic, cross-reference, symbol, dimension, sign, objective, scenario, appendix, and code defects

moves: input: A toll-plaza design must trade accident exposure, traffic flow, and construction footprint while specifying geometry and merging.
rhetorical job: Preview the three-stage model chain, its scenario tests, the New Jersey application, and the authority-facing deliverable in execution order.
analytical job: Attach every headline number to the model or scenario that produces it, keeping lane count, merge flow, accident rate, area, autonomy, and booth mix distinct.
output: A complete decision preview: seven one-way toll lanes in the baseline, a 1375 veh/h route branch, a reported 0.9-0.96% accident rate, a 4650.1875 m2 plaza, and a ten-lane New Jersey case.
handoff: The introduction explains the public-road mechanism, research gap, and four work packages behind the preview.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Retain the source-anchored input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff contract; warnings remain the final pass.

moves: input: Expressway growth makes toll plazas a localized bottleneck where service demand, queueing, fan-in, and unsafe lane changes interact.
rhetorical job: Move from broad transport importance to the toll-plaza failure mechanism, then review capacity and safety studies before stating the synthesis gap and work map.
analytical job: Separate cited background, observed mechanism, literature coverage, unresolved design gap, and the paper's own analytical commitments.
output: A four-part agenda covering toll-lane count, risk-flow merging, minimum-area geometry, and performance under traffic, autonomy, and booth-composition changes.
handoff: The overall/key-point analysis converts that agenda into three decision tensions and a scoped assumption ledger.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Retain the source-anchored input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff contract; warnings remain the final pass.

moves: input: The toll-plaza design must carry vehicles safely from L highway lanes through B service lanes and back while controlling congestion, conflict, and land cost.
rhetorical job: Restate the goal through three key-point subsections so each later model has one visible decision job.
analytical job: Map lane count to demand/service, merging to throughput/safety, and size to following/braking distance and cost.
output: Three typed problem interfaces with distinct inputs, criteria, and downstream models.
handoff: The assumptions and symbol table bound the interfaces before equations are introduced.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Retain the source-anchored input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff contract; warnings remain the final pass.

moves: input: A tractable toll-plaza model requires vehicle classes, speed behavior, roadway condition, directional symmetry, and booth orientation to be fixed.
rhetorical job: Pair every assumption with a stated reason so simplification remains inspectable rather than implicit.
analytical job: Distinguish fleet aggregation, kinematic uniformity, geometric symmetry, and orientation constraints because they fail in different ways.
output: A conditional domain for the queue, network-flow, and area models.
handoff: The notation and overall flow chart expose which variables consume these premises.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Retain the source-anchored input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff contract; warnings remain the final pass.

moves: input: The three model layers exchange demand, capacity, lane count, risk, distance, time, and queue quantities.
rhetorical job: Provide a compact symbol table and a workflow figure before detailed derivations.
analytical job: Keep similar-looking symbols such as N/B, M/c_ij, T_q/T_d, and S'/D' attached to their model roles and units.
output: A typed interface from toll-lane determination through merging and area sizing to parameter checks and the New Jersey case.
handoff: Model I begins by selecting a reasonable number of toll lanes.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Retain the source-anchored input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff contract; warnings remain the final pass.

moves: input: A toll plaza becomes a bottleneck when design-hour demand exceeds capacity at the chosen service level.
rhetorical job: Introduce lane-count logic from qualitative factors, then quantify design-hour volume and single-lane service capacity.
analytical job: Separate forecast demand, charging/service time, and service-level choice before solving for lane count.
output: DHV and single-lane capacity M as inputs to the multi-lane queue model.
handoff: The M/G/K section computes stay, delay, and queue length for candidate N.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Retain the source-anchored input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff contract; warnings remain the final pass.

moves: input: Candidate lane counts must be evaluated under stochastic service and departure time rather than by single-lane capacity multiplication alone.
rhetorical job: Move from expected service/departure moments through queue wait, total stay, queue length, and vehicle delay.
analytical job: Retain each moment, summation limit, lane-count exponent, and stability denominator because small notation changes alter the queue model.
output: T_q, T_d, L_q, and d for each candidate N and arrival intensity lambda.
handoff: Service-level thresholds translate these outputs into a lane-selection rule.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Retain the source-anchored input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff contract; warnings remain the final pass.

moves: input: Queue length and delay must be converted into a service-level criterion and a traffic-intensity lookup for candidate lane counts.
rhetorical job: Explain qualitative level bands, present the intensity table, and derive the hourly throughput inequality before selecting N.
analytical job: Keep q/s, n_N, service time S, DHV, and the table lookup in one auditable chain.
output: A minimum candidate N satisfying the required service level and N' > DHV.
handoff: The worked New Jersey baseline reports seven one-way toll lanes and then tests DHV sensitivity.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Retain the source-anchored input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff contract; warnings remain the final pass.

moves: input: The symbolic lane rule must be instantiated and its response to traffic demand checked.
rhetorical job: Give an algebraic four-step algorithm, report the baseline inputs/result, then vary demand and interpret the plotted staircase.
analytical job: Separate assumed service level and service time from observed or queried traffic volume and from the resulting lane count.
output: A seven-lane one-way baseline and a positive, discrete relationship between hourly traffic and required lanes.
handoff: Model II consumes the selected B while optimizing the merging network.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Retain the source-anchored input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff contract; warnings remain the final pass.

moves: input: Given L main lanes and B toll lanes, post-service vehicles need an explicit network allocation that balances throughput and accident exposure.
rhetorical job: Abstract input, booths, arcs, and merge point into G=(V,A,C), define risk from volume/capacity ratio, combine objectives, and state flow/capacity constraints.
analytical job: Retain the distinction between arc flow H_ij, capacity c_ij/M_ij, accident rate b_ij, net flow v, demand d_i, and penalty lambda.

warnings.warning: Equation (3) uses K-i while the parallel Equation (5) uses N-i; K is not separately defined in this queue factor.
The prose sends queue length to Equation (6), but Equation (5) defines L_q and Equation (6) only adds expectations.
Normality alone does not justify the printed M/G/K form or variance addition; independence, stability, and sample fit are absent.
AADT=38594, K=0.12, and D=0.60 imply about 2778.8 veh/h, not the printed 4578 veh/h.
Equation (21) duplicates flow balance with d_i while Equation (22) defines f_i, leaving the node-supply symbol inconsistent.
Equation (21) does not reconcile M_ij with c_ij or provide lambda's value and unit conversion.
Equation (23) omits a visible km/h-to-m/s conversion under the surrounding speed convention.
Equation (24) contains ambiguous powers and deceleration signs that require a unit-tested reconstruction.
Equation (25) displays max Z although the section frames a minimum-cost and minimum-footprint problem.
Equation (25) gives a_i>0 without a complete acceleration/deceleration sign convention and leaves both weights undefined.
Table 6's risk sequence is nonmonotone even though the prose describes accident rate as increasing with flow.
Base and autonomous route tables both report 0.96 percent, inconsistent with the summary's claimed 0.83 percent reduction.
New Jersey source identity, raw flow, width semantics, and area precision are insufficient to reproduce the application.
Annex 3 repeats a service-level title while displaying a sparse capacity adjacency matrix.
LINGO1 omits +2.7091 and changes the risk denominators to C/263 and C/236.
LINGO1 minimizes sum(u) independent of flow and bounds f by u rather than c, so it does not implement Equation (21).
